newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares surge higher following bonds.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares surge higher following bonds.

text.p: Italian shares ended sharply higher on Wednesday following surging domestic bonds and a firmer lira while the changes to Milan's Mib30 blue-chip index of top Italian shares encouraged buying interest.

The rejigged Mib30 index saw four new entrants - Mediaset, Mediolanum, Banca Fideuram and Saipem, while Compart, Ambroveneto, Ifil and Ifi all dropped out. The bourse also adjusted weighing in the index with ENI, TIM and Telecom Italia gaining while Fiat, Generali and Olivetti lost weight.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 1.91 percent at 9,743 while the Mib30 was 1.97 percent higher at 14,635.

Telecom stocks moved ahead after Tuesday's results from Telecom Italia which showed first-half pretax profits up 27 percent. The shares ended up 1.01 percent at 3,190. TIM rose 3.55 percent to 3,120 lire, while STET closed up 3.0 percent at 4,940 lire just ahead of its results.
Amongst the insurers, RAS moved 4.15 percent ahead to 13,940 lire after showing first half parent company net profit up to 157 billion lire for 154 billion lire.
Agro-industrial group Montedison ended up 3.63 percent at 925 lire. The group reported underlying net first half 1996 profits largely steady after the stock market closed.
Montedison's results were distorted by a massive capital gain made from its Montell deal in early 1995, but stripping this out, the underlying net picture was largely flat.
Compart was up 3.29 percent at 514.5 lire ahead of its results later today.
Among others, Pirelli gained 1.44 percent to 2,673 lire ahead of its first-half result Thursday, while ENI continued to thrive up 3.25 percent at 7,361 lire.
